Name: Performance Plus
Description:
This mod improves performance of Timberborn, mainly through remembering results of previously made searches. It's built on top of T3MP, and in its basic mode it results in gameplay exactly identical to vanilla. Advanced options in mod settings allow you to turn on further optimisations at the cost of minor changes to gameplay.

Adding or removing the mod is safe for saves both ways: it does not change vanilla saves in any way.

Tested on three large settlements (400-600 population, 10 000+ objects), at speed 7 the frame rate increased by up to 20% compared with T3MP alone, and up to 30% with the minor gameplay changes optimisations.

[h2]List of optimisations (for nerds)[/h2]
[h3]1. Paths[/h3]
[list]
[*]1.1 Path questions asked again before the paths have changed are answered from memory instead of being worked out again.
[*]1.2 A path to an object reachable from all sides (construction sites, piles, demolition jobs) is remembered as one answer instead of one per side.
[*]1.3 When the paths change, only the affected remembered road search trees are thrown away.
[*]1.4 Changes to where beavers may wander no longer throw away the remembered paths, since only wandering reads them.
[*]1.5 The game's record of which places can reach which is kept in arrays instead of a dictionary (since keys were consecutive numbers), so it is rebuilt faster after every change to the paths.
[*]1.6 Paths are not checked tile by tile for gates (which affect walking speed) while the settlement has no gate.
[/list]

[h3]2. Builders[/h3]
[list]
[*]2.1 A builder looking for work finds its hub's district once per search, not once for every construction site.
[*]2.2 Builders know which construction sites are switched on without asking every site again on every search.
[*]2.3 Builders' searches walk only the sites that are switched on, and a site's list of accessible sides rewritten with the same sides keeps its remembered paths.
[*]2.4 Each construction site remembers its path from every builder hub (up to 32), not just from the last one that asked.
[*]2.5 A construction site checks whether enough build time has been put in before its other finishing checks.
[*]2.6 Construction sites whose missing goods are nowhere in stock in the district are passed over until some come in or the site's inventory changes.
[/list]

[h3]3. Lumberjacks and demolition[/h3]
[list]
[*]3.1 A lumberjack looks only at the marked trees its flag can reach, from a list kept per flag, instead of every marked tree on the map.
[*]3.2 Those per-flag lists are rebuilt only after relevant path changes and skip unnecessary indirection.
[*]3.3 A builder choosing something to demolish asks first whether it is nearer than the best so far, before checking other (costlier) conditions.
[*]3.4 The demolition search remembers whether a demolish job is reachable instead of looking it up again on every search.
[/list]

[h3]4. Farms, foresters and gatherers[/h3]
[list]
[*]4.1 Farmers and foresters go through their spots nearest first and stop at the first they may plant, skipping spots taken by a crop or tree.
[*]4.2 A forester replanting dead trees asks only the spots where a dead tree stands.
[*]4.3 A farmer whose farm house has no room for [i]any[/i] good grown in its range does not search the crops for one to harvest.
[*]4.4 A farm house with no room for any of the [i]ripe[/i] crops' goods does not search its crops again until it has room or another crop ripens.
[*]4.5 Kinds of crops and trees in range are remembered instead of being looked up every time.
[*]4.6 When a tree or crop in a building's range is removed, only the decision about whether to still accept that one good into inventory is updated, not every good in range.
[/list]

[h3]5. Goods[/h3]
[list]
[*]5.1 A carrier asked to fill an inventory with no room left for the good does not search the district's stock first.
[*]5.2 An inventory's (e.g. warehouse's) fill percentages are remembered until its stock, capacity or allowed goods change, instead of being recomputed, by a loop over every good it may hold, each time it is asked.
[*]5.3 A district's stock and capacity counts are updated by the inventories or buildings that changed, instead of recounted from every inventory every tick.
[/list]

[h3]6. Beavers, bots and other objects[/h3]
[list]
[*]6.1 A beaver entering a building has its model switched on or off at most once, instead of twice which is costly in Unity.
[*]6.2 A beaver's behaviour log is converted to string when the save or the debug panel reads it, not at every change of behaviour.
[*]6.3 Whether a new or removed object is a tube is asked once overall, not once per beaver. Every beaver reuses that answer in reacting to the object.
[*]6.4 A removed object is found in the game's list of all objects by direct identity/reference comparison, not by the list's slower general search that uses general equality.
[*]6.5 An object remembers its own status warnings and removes them directly when the object is removed, instead of looking through the list of all statuses to identify its own. The warnings panel is rebuilt from the active warnings only, instead of asking every object that could possibly have active warnings if it actually has any.
[/list]

[h3]7. Water[/h3]
[list]
[*]7.1 All objects that react to water are kept in an array of their positions and checked against a corresponding array of water heights. Objects are only touched when the water height actually changes.
[*]7.2 The water's look is sent to the graphics card once a frame instead of once a step, since only a frame's last step is drawn.
[*]7.3 The water's previous-step layers are not sent again when the graphics card already holds them.
[/list]

[h3]8. Drawing and sound[/h3]
[list]
[*]8.1 Power shafts' animations are set once a frame instead of once a step.
[*]8.2 A beaver (animated model) choosing its next animation copies its parameters (walking, carrying, etc.) from dictionary to an array and chooses the right animation based on that array.
[*]8.3 Animated models out of the camera's sight keep their animation time but are posed only when they come into sight.
[*]8.4 Beavers out of the camera's sight skip the per-frame swimming update until they could be seen.
[*]8.5 The point sounds are heard from is looked for again only when the camera moves, the window changes size, or every eighth frame.
[*]8.6 Recoloured materials, such as tubeway lights, are remembered so the same colouring is not looked up again.
[/list]

[h2]9. Additional options (Mod Settings, all off by default)[/h2]
[list]
[*]9.1 [b]Allow minor gameplay changes[/b]: faster shortcuts that change small details, such as hauling-post workers choosing from a job list up to half an hour old.
[*]9.3 [b]Shorter shadow distance[/b]: shadows only up to 60 m from the camera. A middle option between vanilla options of shadows on and off.
[*]9.4 [b]Animate distant models less often[/b]: animations for beavers and buildings far away skip some frames, depending on how small they are.
[*]9.5 [b]Keep a frame rate[/b]: slows the game below the speed you chose when frames would take too long to preserve the requested frame rate.
[*]9.2 [b]Tick length (%)[/b] (minor gameplay change): longer simulation steps (120% to 300%, in steps that fit a day exactly), so the game keeps up at high speeds. Rates of gameplay mechanics are adjusted accordingly to be the same per day; slightly delays beaver decisions, which leads to minor inefficiencies.
[*]9.6 [b]Tick length follows the frame rate[/b]: an extra to "Keep a frame rate" and "Tick length (%)", the set tick length is the longest a step gets. The game starts at 100% and every day the step grows or shrinks one notch if needed, based on the prior day.
[/list]

[h2]Dependencies[/h2]
Requires T3MP, Harmony and Mod Settings.
